import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        group0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
        group1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
        effect = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect))
    
    # Rank features by effect size
    ranked_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top candidates, avoiding near-duplicates
    selected = []
    used_ids = set()
    
    # Check correlations to avoid near-duplicates
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for idx in ranked_indices:
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        if fid in used_ids:
            continue
            
        # Add this feature and mark correlated features as used
        selected.append(fid)
        used_ids.add(fid)
        
        # Mark correlated features as used
        for j, other_fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
            if i != j and abs(corr_matrix[idx, j]) >= corr_threshold:
                used_ids.add(other_fid)
                
        if len(selected) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
            break
    
    # If no strong drivers found, return empty design
    if not selected:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # For logistic regression, include all selected features plus interactions
    columns = tuple(selected)
    products = ()
    loadings = {fid: 1.0 for fid in selected}
    
    # Check for interaction terms (strongest two features)
    if len(selected) >= 2:
        # Simple approach: use top 2 features for interaction
        a, b = selected[:2]
        products = ((a, b),)
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(selected), columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
